title: One-Pot Creamy Tomato & Spinach Ravioli
description: Refrigerated cheese ravioli cooks right in a simple tomato sauce with spinach for a low-effort weeknight dinner.
substitutions: Use frozen ravioli and add a few extra minutes of covered cooking.
Use chopped frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry.
Leave out mozzarella for an even simpler dinner.

steps.text: Simmer the ravioli in tomato sauce.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 jar pasta sauce and 1 cup water in a large deep skillet and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add 20 ounces refrigerated cheese ravioli. Cover and simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring gently once or twice, until the ravioli are tender.
Stir in 3 cups baby spinach and 1/2 cup milk. Cook uncovered 2–3 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the sauce is hot.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup mozzarella if using, cover for 1–2 minutes to melt, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water or milk until steaming hot.

title: Ham, Cheddar & Apple Pinwheels
description: Ham, cheddar, and crisp apple roll into soft tortillas for a no-cook lunch that is easy to pack or make at home.

ingredients.item: apple, cut into very thin matchsticks

substitutions: Use deli turkey instead of ham.
Use a pear instead of apple.
Use mayonnaise if you do not have cream cheese.

cookSteps.text: Lay out 2 large tortillas. Spread each with 1 tablespoon cream cheese or mayonnaise and 1/2 teaspoon mustard if using.
Divide 4 ounces deli ham, 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, and 1/2 small apple cut into thin matchsticks between the tortillas.
Roll each tortilla up tightly. Place seam-side down and slice each roll into 5 or 6 pinwheels.
Serve right away, or chill until lunch.

storage: Refrigerate tightly covered up to 24 hours for best texture.

title: Leftover Baked Potato & Broccoli Soup
description: Cold baked potatoes turn into a quick creamy broccoli soup instead of becoming a forgotten leftover.
substitutions: Use leftover boiled or roasted potatoes.
Use frozen cauliflower instead of broccoli.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Simmer the broccoli and leftover potatoes.
Mash lightly and finish with milk and cheese.

cookSteps.text: Cut 2 cooked baked potatoes into chunks. Put them in a saucepan with 2 cups frozen broccoli, 2 cups broth, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder if using.
Bring to a simmer and cook 8–10 minutes, until the broccoli is tender and everything is steaming hot.
Mash some of the potatoes and broccoli with a potato masher or fork, leaving plenty of texture.
Stir in 1 cup milk and heat gently for 2–3 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in 3/4 cup cheddar, season to taste, and serve.

storage: Use leftover potatoes only while they are within their original safe refrigerated storage window. Refrigerate the finished soup up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Chocolate Chip Bread Pudding Mugs
description: A few slices of stale bread become two warm chocolate-chip bread puddings without making a full pan.

ingredients.item: cubed stale sandwich bread or brioche

substitutions: Use raisins instead of chocolate chips.
Use white or wheat sandwich bread, brioche, or soft dinner rolls.
Leave out cinnamon or vanilla if you do not have them.

steps.text: Soak stale bread in a simple custard.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease 2 oven-safe mugs or small ramekins and set them on a small baking pan.
Whisk 1 egg, 3/4 cup milk, 3 tablespoons brown sugar, and the vanilla and cinnamon if using in a mixing bowl.
Fold in 3 cups stale bread cubes and 3 tablespoons chocolate chips. Let the mixture stand 5 minutes so the bread can absorb the custard.
Divide between the 2 mugs or ramekins. Bake 16–18 minutes, until puffed and set in the center.
Cool for 5 minutes before eating; the centers stay very hot.

storage: Refrigerate covered up to 3 days. Reheat gently until hot throughout.
